_comment: Proof unit produced by the content factory. povQuestions.json-compatible 'image scenario': one validated illustration carrying a bank of mixed-format, age-laddered questions. readClarity reflects coach-gate status.
readTrigger: The defender's stick and lead skate are committed to the puck-side shooting lane, sealing the shot; the weak-side seam to the back-door teammate (#23) is unobstructed; the goalie is squared to the puck carrier and has not started sliding across.
distractors: Goalie squared to the puck (tempts a shot); open ice to the wide side (tempts driving wide); defender still visually 'in the play' (tempts a deke).

groundTruth.correctRead: Cross-ice pass to the back-door teammate (#23).

actors.you: #7, puck carrier, strong side, entering the offensive zone.
actors.teammate: #23, weak side, streaking to the back door, OPEN.
actors.defender: #6, lone D, COMMITTED to the puck/shot side (stick + lead skate in the shooting lane), seam to #23 vacated.
actors.goalie: #30, squared and slightly deep to #7, has not started sliding.

artBrief: See PROOF-2on1-crossice.md section 2. Fixed STYLE/RINK/JERSEYS blocks for library consistency; SITUATION block commits the defender to remove ambiguity.

questions.questionText: You have the puck on a 2-on-1. Read the defender, then make your play.
questions.explanation: The defender's stick and lead skate are in your shooting lane, sealing the shot. The seam to #23 is unguarded and the goalie hasn't moved. Move the puck.

questions.questionText: Tap the player you should move the puck to.
questions.explanation: #23 is open on the back door because the defender committed to your shot. Put it on his tape.
questions.buildNote: All listed targets must be tappable, or this degrades to a coin-flip.

questions.questionText: The defender is in your shooting lane. Shooting is still the best choice here.
questions.explanation: A committed defender plus a square goalie make the shot low-percentage. The open man is the play.

questions.questionText: Your teammate is wide open on the far side. The defender is moving to block your shot. What should you do?

options.label: C
options.text: Try to go around the defender

questions.explanation: The defender is taking your shot away and your teammate is all alone. Passing is the smart, easy play.

questions.questionText: You have the puck. Your friend is open. What do you do?
questions.explanation: Your friend is open! Sharing the puck is the best play.

questions.questionText: You decide to shoot instead of pass. Given the defender's position, what is the MOST likely result?

options.label: B
options.text: The defender blocks or deflects the shot

options.label: D
options.text: The goalie freezes it for a whistle

questions.explanation: His stick and skate are already in the lane. Shooting into a committed defender usually ends in a block or deflection.

questions.questionText: Before you pass, what tells you the back door is truly open?

options.label: A
options.text: The defender's stick and skate are in your shooting lane, leaving the cross-ice seam unguarded

options.label: B
options.text: The goalie is cheating to your side

questions.explanation: The seam is open because the defender vacated it — that's the primary cue. The goalie being square only tells you the shot is contested.

questions.questionText: Given that the defender has committed to your shooting lane, a cross-ice pass to #23 is too risky and should be avoided.
questions.explanation: Because the defender committed to the puck, the seam is open — the pass is the correct read here, not a reckless one.
